raw_record.support_text: Isoniazid (INH) causes human drug-induced liver injury with a delayed onset; anti-INH and/or anti-P450 antibodies were found in 15 of 19 patients with INH-induced liver failure, and covalent INH binding was identified in a human liver biopsy from a patient with INH-induced liver failure. In five patients with mild INH-induced liver injury there was an increase in Th17 cells and IL-10-producing cells, whereas patients taking INH without liver injury showed none of these findings. The authors conclude the mechanism is immune-mediated idiosyncratic injury rather than 'metabolic idiosyncrasy.'
raw_record.extra_details: Delayed-onset liver injury; mild injury can resolve despite continued treatment. Anti-INH and/or anti-P450 antibodies detected in serum of 15/19 patients with INH-induced liver failure, but no anti-drug or anti-P450 antibodies in patients who received INH without severe liver injury. Increased Th17 and IL-10-producing cells in 5 patients with mild INH-induced liver injury. Covalent binding of INH identified in a human liver biopsy from a patient with INH-induced liver failure. Authors reject prior 'metabolic idiosyncrasy' mechanism attributed to acetylhydrazine (AcHz) bioactivation.

raw_record.support_text: Among 27 DILI patients analyzed, a unique case of acute hepatic failure was caused by abusive consumption of paracetamol (APAP) over time, without other relevant comorbidities. The 40-year-old male patient presented with hypotension, drowsiness, peripheral cyanosis, icterus, right upper quadrant abdominal pain, and altered laboratory values (AST > 4,600 U/L, creatinine 4.6 mg/dL). Serum APAP at admission (220 μg/mL) indicated possible liver toxicity, N-acetylcysteine was given, and post-mortem liver analysis 2 days after admission showed extensive necrosis, congestion, infiltration, hemorrhage and ischaemia, all signs compatible with a hepatotoxic etiology.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Chronic abusive (supratherapeutic) consumption over time; single male patient (40 years) with several prior suicide attempts; no other relevant comorbidities.
raw_record.extra_details: Patient presented with hypotension (blood pressure 70/40), drowsiness, peripheral cyanosis, conjunctival icterus, right upper quadrant abdominal pain; laboratory values AST > 4,600 U/L, creatinine 4.6 mg/dL, leukocytosis; serum APAP concentration 220 μg/mL at admission (>4 h post ingestion), indicating possible liver toxicity by the Rumack-Matthew nomogram. Treated with N-acetylcysteine. Post-mortem liver examination showed extensive necrosis, congestion, infiltration, hemorrhage and ischaemia.
